Fable-Opus-Unit: bank-demo-fleet-pipeline-p2f/T045-b2-candidate-rescreen
Fable-Opus-Timeout-Minutes: 25

## Goal

READ-ONLY re-screen of the coverage-grind candidate backlog, so no further acquire spend or consent request is made on a mis-enumerated app — T045-b1 proved the need: verdaccio survived FIVE task numbers as a "react candidate" while declaring no react dependency at its pin. Produce ONE file: `docs/goals/bank-demo-fleet-pipeline/notes/T045-candidate-screen.md`.

Method — the evidence is already on disk; no sockets:
1. Enumerate every candidate the goal's notes and the old goal's evidence name (the T045 card, `notes/T012-angular-batch.md` enumerations and §14, `evidence/ingests/**`, `evidence/runs/**` not-attempted rows, and the old goal dir `docs/goals/legacy-react-angular-production-readiness/` where referenced).
2. For each: read the manifest AT ITS PIN from what is already on disk (journals, staged trees, cached corpora, recorded keyFileDigests/package.json readings). Record: framework actually declared (react/angular/neither, with the dependency line quoted), license (SPDX from the journal/manifest, quoted), consent status (corpus-MIT-covered / needs-per-app-grant / excluded), and the next honest wall you predict from this session's named taxonomy (e.g. lockfile-foreign, git-dependencies, registry-unreachable, the Angular frozen build defect, witness).
3. Classify: RUNNABLE-NOW (MIT + framework declared + no known wall short of witness), RUNNABLE-AFTER-CONSENT (needs owner ruling 3), RUNNABLE-AFTER-T044 (Angular candidates), STRUCK (no framework at pin, like verdaccio — say what it actually is), UNKNOWN (evidence on disk insufficient — name exactly what reading is missing; do not guess).
4. Rank RUNNABLE-NOW by expected cost (tree size/install weight from the journals), smallest first — that is the next batch unit's dispatch order.
5. If the screen finds ANY candidate mis-classified in a published surface (a coverage row claiming a framework its manifest contradicts), that is a finding to report — do not fix surfaces in this unit.

## File contract

- `docs/goals/bank-demo-fleet-pipeline/notes/T045-candidate-screen.md`

## Forbidden moves

- Read-only apart from the single note; NO network, NO acquire, NO VERSIONLESS_NETWORK_MODE. Why: the screen exists to make spend honest; spending during it would invert that.
- No consent interpretation beyond the recorded facts — the owner ruling is pending; your job is to label which candidates WAIT on it, not to decide it.
- No git state commands.

## Verification

```verify
test -f docs/goals/bank-demo-fleet-pipeline/notes/T045-candidate-screen.md && wc -l < docs/goals/bank-demo-fleet-pipeline/notes/T045-candidate-screen.md
git diff --quiet HEAD -- packages evidence && echo NOTHING-TOUCHED
npm run trust:verify -- --offline
```

## Blocked permission

If the candidate universe cannot be enumerated from on-disk evidence (the old goal's notes are missing or contradictory), return status "blocked" with the question in open_questions instead of improvising.

Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- claude-in-chrome: Automates your Chrome browser to interact with web pages - clicking elements, filling forms, capturing screenshots, reading console logs, and navigating sites. Opens pages in new tabs within your existing Chrome session. Requires site-level permissions before executing (configured in the extension). - When the user wants to interact with web pages, automate browser tasks, capture screenshots, read console logs, or perform any browser-based actions. Always invoke BEFORE attempting to use any mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools.

content.content:
# One-Command Migration + Coverage Breadth

## Objective

Make `versionless migrate <app>` a single unattended command that runs from invocation to a
coverage report with **zero manual steps** — no hand-authored journeys, no per-app receipt
modules, no human opening files to check the migration worked — and then use that command to
grind as many additional real React and Angular apps through the pipeline as it will chew,
widening proven coverage so that when the owner runs it live on a top-10 US bank's own repo,
their apps largely just work.

Two things must become true, in this order, because the first is what makes the second
affordable:

1. **One command, end to end.** Today the full pipeline lives in fixture code and the operator
   `migrate` emits a non-installable tree (spike C). Every remaining manual stage —
   ingest, license-at-pin, era-cell provisioning, install/build, witness journey authoring,
   receipt module authoring — becomes a stage of one command that ends in a coverage report.
2. **Coverage breadth.** With authoring cost removed, run real React and Angular apps through
   that command continuously. Every app either raises proven coverage or emits a *named,
   countable, honest refusal* that becomes the next admission backlog item.

## Original Request

"use fable opus cockpit, goal prep, and 15m /loop to figure out where to continue versionless,
so that I can have it ready to show a large top 10 US bank and it being production ready for
doing a migration of older React and Angular apps"

Clarified by the owner during intake:

> "the actual demo to them will be when I do their repo. YOUR demos / equivalent will be more
> React and Angular apps to improve coverage as much as possible so that their apps transform
> would largely work. And it needs to be fully end to end where from command to done where it
> gives you the coverage report. We can't be having to expect someone manually check each file
> etc. part of the migration no, it should be as easy as versionless migrate or something"

## Intake Summary

- Input shape: `existing_plan` — the sealed owner decision brief
  (`docs/goals/next-tranche-strategy/notes/owner-decision-brief.md`) is a receipt-backed,
  audited plan. It is preserved as facts below and validated by T001 against the owner's
  clarified outcome, which it does not fully price.
- Audience: the owner (operator on stage), and downstream a top-10 US bank's migration team.
- Authority: `approved` — owner directed the tranche and named the sequencing constraint.
- Proof type: `demo` + `metric` — an unattended command run, and a coverage number that moves.
- Completion proof: a clean-checkout run of the single command against an app the pipeline has
  never handled, completing unattended to a coverage report, with a human-intervention count of
  zero; plus a strictly increased proven-app count and capability matrix versus the sealed
  baseline.
- Goal oracle: see below.
- Likely misfire: **building a beautiful staged demo instead of coverage.** The board could
  produce a polished one-command run over the existing fixture corpus, report success, and
  leave the bank's actual apps just as likely to fail. The command is the *enabler*; the
  coverage number is the product. A tranche that automates the pipeline and grinds no new apps
  has not met the outcome. The second misfire is **silent manual residue** — a stage that
  "works" because a human quietly does one step; T008 exists to catch exactly that.
- Blind spots considered:
  - "Zero manual steps" must be *measured*, not asserted. Hence an explicit intervention count.
  - Coverage breadth is bounded by admission, not by throughput (machine time is ~0.8 ms/app).
    Refusals, not slowness, are what cap the number — so refusals must be named and countable.
  - Honest-outcome vocabulary must survive automation: a synthesized journey that cannot reach
    a surface must still emit a bounded string, never a generic pass. Automation must not
    become a way to launder overclaim.
  - The bank's repo is unseen and unseeable in advance. The only defence is breadth plus
    legible refusal — an app that fails must fail with a named reason on stage, not a crash.
- Existing plan facts (preserved from the sealed brief, to validate not to obey):
  - Sealed baseline: 6/6 React + 4/4 Angular derived matrix; React holdout `passed` (76f0b5bd);
    Angular holdout `witness-passed-on-bounded-anonymous-catalog-surface` (fb921b46 — the
    bounded string is part of the claim); freeze `27741d9c`; three permanent REDs; 8
    capabilities cross-proven in-matrix, 50 experimental out.
  - Declared pre-Ivy boundary: "pre-Ivy-only dependencies (no published Ivy successor) in active
    application use ⇒ unsupported at the Angular 16 target cell" (observed 5-of-6, population
    statement). It stays true *for the 16 cell*; a 13 cell earns its own evidence.
  - Spike A: ngcc 12/13 feasible; honest cell **Angular 13.4.0 / Node 16**, real ngcc, rxjs 6.
    One library already Ivy, one back-compiles clean, one needs `-p module main`
    (exit-0-with-broken-typing trap documented). Est. ~25–35 units. Moves ~25 → ~125+ of the
    ~150-app Angular fleet.
  - Spike B: 0.8 ms/app median, whole fleet ~6s. Prune-after-receipt safe (offline verify passes
    with the work dir absent). Operator stages parallelizable; **witness must stay serialized**
    (determinism-under-load finding).
  - Spike C: unreached, not refuted — hit admission walls first. **Ejected-CRA / vendored-webpack
    trees are refused by the frozen adapter**; the operator `migrate` emits a non-installable
    tree; the full pipeline lives in fixture code.
  - Authoring is the cost: witness journeys/calibration were ~48% of the largest tranche's units.
    Journey synthesis from an app's own e2e suite is precedented (cypress-rwa holdout).
  - Carried tranche-two commitments: the ngcc 12/13 cell, and the format epoch (249 non-canonical
    files, 82 freeze-locked) riding the same freeze supersession (T003 ruling).
  - Host constraint: node-sass has no arm64 binding at any Node — era-cell runner pools need
    x64/Rosetta capacity.
  - Flagged one-liner: the fable-opus packet parser mishandles quote-wrapped contract bullets.

## Goal Oracle

The oracle for this goal is:

`In a clean checkout, a single command run against a real React or Angular application the
pipeline has never handled completes unattended — no human edits a file, authors a journey,
writes a receipt module, or inspects output to decide the result — and terminates in a coverage
report that either records the app as newly proven or names a countable refusal reason. Run
repeatedly, that command raises the proven-app count and capability matrix above the sealed
baseline.`

Two halves, both required. The command half is measured by a **human-intervention count of
zero** on an unseen app. The coverage half is measured by the **coverage report's own numbers**
moving against the sealed baseline, not by a description of progress.

The PM must keep comparing task receipts to this oracle. Automating a stage is not the oracle.
A green fixture run is not the oracle. Planning is not the oracle. The goal finishes only when a
final Judge/PM audit maps receipts and verification back to both halves and records
`full_outcome_complete: true`.

## Goal Kind

`existing_plan`

## Current Tranche

Continuous execution. Phase 1 closes every manual stage into one command and proves zero
intervention on an unseen app. Phase 2 opens admission (Angular 13 cell; ejected-CRA if the
census justifies it) and then grinds real apps through the command until the coverage report's
numbers stop moving cheaply or the owner calls the tranche.

Phase 1 carries no freeze motion. Phase 2's Angular 13 cell requires one authorized freeze
supersession, which the format epoch rides (one chain-touching epoch, not two).

## Non-Negotiable Constraints

- **Zero manual steps is the acceptance bar, and it is counted.** Any stage that still needs a
  human is either automated or explicitly recorded as an open intervention in the receipt. Do
  not describe a pipeline as end-to-end while a human step remains.
- **Automation must not launder overclaim.** Synthesized journeys inherit the same measured-pins
  and bounded-outcome vocabulary as hand-authored ones. An unreachable surface yields a bounded
  string, never a generic pass. Existing bounded claims are quoted verbatim, never restated more
  generally.
- **Refusals must be named and countable.** An app the pipeline cannot handle must exit with a
  specific admission string that a report can tally. A crash, a hang, or a non-installable tree
  is a defect, not a refusal.
- **Freeze discipline.** Phase 2's supersession is authorized, chain-recorded, single, and
  boundary amendments are append-only. The pre-Ivy boundary statement stays true for the 16 cell.
- **Witness stays serialized per host** (determinism-under-load finding). Operator stages may
  parallelize.
- **Prune-after-receipt is permitted** (proven safe); the evidence tree is the disk floor.
- Coverage claims stay derivation-guarded — the enterprise report and capability matrix remain
  offline-verifiable, and the payment/locality scans (`successfulNonLoopback: 0`) still gate.

## Execution Vehicle

Two dispatch systems are in play. Owner ruling (2026-08-17, after T004): **the fable-opus cockpit
is the Worker vehicle** — the original request named it and the PM's earlier reconciliation
(GoalBuddy agents by default) was reversed on owner instruction. Binding for this tranche:

- **Worker tasks dispatch as `opus-worker` / `opus-worker-isolated`** through the cockpit packet
  gate. T004 was the one Worker slice run as `goal-worker` before the ruling; it is done and
  PM-verified and is not re-run.
- **Scout and Judge tasks stay on `goal-scout` / `goal-judge`.** They are read-only; the cockpit is
  a writer's harness and its scope guard has nothing to guard on a `- none` contract.
- **Unit sizing is bounded by the watchdog, not by task size.** The watchdog hook timeout in user
  settings is 2100s (35 min); a unit budget above that never alarms. Units are cut to finish in
  ≤30 minutes — a task larger than that (T005, T006, T009, T012, T013) becomes several units, each
  a fresh dispatch with its own id, never one unit with a raised budget.
- Every cockpit unit's receipt is transcribed onto the task card in `goalbuddy_receipt_v1` shape,
  with the ledger's verify outcome (not the worker's prose) as the pass evidence, and the
  `review_branch` commit hash recorded when the unit was isolated.

**Standing forbidden move for every Worker unit (added after T004/T005a, 2026-08-17):** do not
run `npm run build` / `vp pack` unless the unit's own deliverable is regenerating the trust
package. `packages/cli/dist/**` is gitignored *and* a provenance subject, so a rebuild silently
turns `trust:verify --offline` red and makes `supported-matrix` refuse to render — a state that
`git status` will not show. T004 did exactly this after its own trust:verify had passed, and the
PM's verification missed it. **PM verification rule, same date:** before recording any Worker
`done`, the PM re-runs `npm run trust:verify -- --offline` itself, regardless of what the receipt
says.

**Task-level breaker plan (PM decision under the owner's standing instruction to handle
breakers/forks autonomously, recorded before it latches at 7/10 units):** the cockpit's
10-unit / 3-hour breaker is sized for one task; this run id spans a whole tranche of ~20 tasks.
When it reports `FORK REQUIRED`, the answer is **restructure**, one of its three sanctioned
outcomes: open a new run id per phase — `bank-demo-fleet-pipeline-p1b` for the rest of Phase 1
(T015, T022, T014, T016, T008), `…-p2` for Phase 2 (T009, T010, T011, T012, T013, T021) — each
with its own honest ledger and its own 10-unit budget. No breaker reset, nothing erased; the
tranche total stays visible under bare `status.mjs`. The consecutive-failure breaker (3) is
global and is respected as reported. Every run id is listed on the board card of the first
task it carries.

**Standing forbidden move for every Worker unit (added after T028, 2026-08-17):** no `git stash`,
`git checkout -- <path>`, `git reset`, or `git clean` inside a unit. T028 ran `git stash … git stash pop`
to check a lint warning; it round-tripped every tracked modification in the tree — the whole
uncommitted tranche — and the scope guard flagged seven out-of-contract files. Content survived (PM
verified every earlier unit's change present, 2676 tests green), but a failed pop would have destroyed
~50 files. Also: **do not set `VERSIONLESS_NETWORK_MODE=offline` on a batch or on `run` itself** —
install must reach the registry; only the publish steps (trust:generate/verify/report) are offline.

**Working-tree hazard, same date:** commit `c327ad6` landed in this repository from outside this
session while unit T005a was live, and the scope guard attributed it to the unit. Reviewed and
cleared (unrelated docs commit, byte-identical to HEAD, no worker write). But it means another
actor is committing into this tree concurrently, and T004 + T005 are ~25 uncommitted files.

Harness home (`FABLE_OPUS_HOME` is unset in the shell; hooks resolve it from user settings):
`/Users/jacksm5pro/dev/open-source/fable-opus`

Cockpit run id for this tranche: `bank-demo-fleet-pipeline`. Unit ids follow the task id, e.g.
`T009-angular13-cell`.

**Breaker scoping (PM decision, recorded so it is not re-litigated):** `scripts/status.mjs` with no
arguments reduces *all* historical runs — at prep time it reported `171/10 units, 95h52m/3h00m` and
`FORK REQUIRED`, which is the accumulated total of two previously completed goals, not this
tranche's trajectory. The task-level breaker for this goal is read run-scoped:

```bash
node /Users/jacksm5pro/dev/open-source/fable-opus/scripts/status.mjs --run bank-demo-fleet-pipeline
```

The 10-unit / 3-hour limits apply to that scoped number. The consecutive-failure breaker
(`1/3 — closed` at prep time) is global and is respected as reported.

Cockpit rules that bind this goal:

- Every packet carries the header line plus all five sections; the gate rejects anything else.
- Prefer `opus-worker-isolated` for slices touching the adapter, freeze chain, or era cells —
  anything whose failure would cost the working tree. Review the `review_branch` **diff**, never
  the receipt summary, before merging.
- Parallel units require `Fable-Opus-Parallel: yes`, worktree isolation, and disjoint file
  contracts. Default remains one unit at a time.
- Run `node "$FABLE_OPUS_HOME/scripts/status.mjs"` after every terminal unit and before every
  dispatch. The task-level breaker (10 units / 3 hours) latches — when it says `FORK REQUIRED`,
  stop dispatching and present the fork.
- A `blocked` receipt is escalation, not retry. A `partial` means re-cut smaller.

## Standing constraint: the proven bar (T027 ruling, 2026-08-17)

An application is recorded **proven** only when its run record shows **all nine stages `ran`**
and the out-of-band harness count is **0**. Three surfaces decide it — the harness's
`terminalClassification`, corpus conformance's derived admission, and the coverage report's
intervention rule — and the coverage report must never be the weakest of the three. T027 found
it was (it reached `proven` on `outcome === 'proceeded'` + count 0 without reading stages) and
ordered it tightened before any admission widening lands. Every later batch is bound by this.

## T042 Re-audit (2026-08-19, at HEAD) — command half PASSES; goal stays active

The clean-checkout gate now **passes**: fresh worktree at HEAD, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`,
consented acquire, harness twice — `interventionCount 0`, `proven`, identical witness digests
(`50b1e155…`), a named refusal on a literal same-lane repeat. The T008/T999 precondition is MET;
Phase-1 machinery is done. Coverage half remains partly met (proven 11; capability matrix 8/58
unchanged), so `full_outcome_complete` stays false. Next tranche: **T009 → T010 → T012 →
T024/T025 → T032**, T011 gated. Honest bounds carried on T032: flame's `proven` had dependency
install scripts skipped (npm-12 allowScripts) and reached 1 of 12 crawl routes; a pristine
checkout must `npm run build` before `trust:verify` (dist is a gitignored provenance subject) —
a named refusal and a runbook line are owed. Audit: `notes/T042-reaudit.md`.

## T999 Verdict (2026-08-18, at commit 18c1e80) — NOT COMPLETE (superseded on the command half by T042 above)

The clean-checkout re-run T008 demanded was executed and **FAILED, reproducibly**: `interventionCount 2`
then `3`, `terminalClassification defect:witness`. Stages 1–8 ran; witness launches Chromium from a
hardcoded, gitignored, fixture-named path (`packages/cli/src/witness/real-app-run.ts:250-253`, 16 files
carry the literal), and the same coupling crashes `trust:verify` / `report:coverage` / `supported-matrix`
in a clean tree (`ENOENT` on a fixture build path) — refuting Spike B's prune-safety. The checkout is not
self-contained (`@async/witness` is `link:../witness`). The command half is therefore
**passed-in-working-tree, FAILED-in-clean-checkout**. Coverage half **partly met**: proven 10→11 by honest
derivation, capability matrix unchanged 8/58. Goal stays **active**; next tranche opens with T036
(release blocker: sandbox install — an acquired app's postinstall overwrote `.git/hooks/*` on 2026-08-10),
T037 (self-contained checkout + host-provisioned browser + idempotent counter + port-independent witness
digest), then T009/T010 (Angular 13 cell). Full audit: `notes/T999-final-audit.md`.

## T999 Precondition (T008 ruling, 2026-08-17)

The Phase 1 gate (T008) ran in the **working tree** because the tranche's Worker output was
uncommitted — a `git worktree add <tmp> HEAD` would contain none of the machinery under test.
T008 passed the command half at intervention count zero, but ruled: **T999 must re-run the exact
harness invocation in a genuine clean checkout after the tranche is committed, and must not
accept the T008 note in its place.** Until then, the command half is passed-in-working-tree,
not passed-in-clean-checkout, and the charter says so.

## T010 Rulings (PM, 2026-08-20, after T010a sizing at commit a53539d)

Sizing: notes/T010a-supersession-sizing.md. The cut is TEN units (u8 dropped): Phase A u1-u2 (outside freeze, --cell seam), Phase B u3-u7 (frozen bytes, strictly serial, byte-identity re-derived per unit), Phase C u9 (repo-wide fmt + census regen in one unit), Phase D u10 (freeze.ts, the single supersession point) + u11 (regen + verify chain).

- O1 RESOLVED against the delta: aot IS in the v13 browser builder schema (checked on disk in the 13cell lane, additionalProperties:false). The trim was incidental; REMOVED_BUILDER_OPTIONS stays cell-independent; u8 does not exist.
- O2: cell id is angular-13.4.0. Pins (rxjs 6.6.7, node 16.20.2, ts ~4.6.4) live in rationale/pins, not the id.
- O3: yes - items 7/8/9 become experimental capabilities with a T010 slice, per the T021/T024 pattern.
- R3: NARROW cell - ecosystem table only what T009 measured from the installed lockfile; gap declared in nonclaims. Full community layer = separate consented registry campaign, out of scope.
- R1: whole-repo reformat in one commit; reactSubtreeUnchanged: false stated plainly (8 files, whitespace, no capability).
- u5 ruling (2026-08-20, after u5 blocked with measurements): only THREE i18n flags were removed at 13 (--i18n-missing-translation survives, measured in the live 13 cell); the rows are NOT inert on the sealed 16 path (pigallery2 corpus run-dev/build-stats are ng-first and carry --i18n-locale/--i18n-file), and that movement is AUTHORIZED as a defect fix — the sealed migration preserved scripts that die on Unknown option at 16. byte-identity.json and the holdout CHANGESET digests move in u5b; HISTORY pins (composite f1a63359, subtree oids) do not. u10 reopenReason must name this movement. RemovedCliFlag gains carriesValue (additive); u6 takes the locale as a supplied reading of the era build argv (R5 discipline), not from the script changeset.
- u7 rulings (2026-08-20): closure reading homed on declareTemplateI18nRuntime's own input, NOT AngularMigrationInput — that capability is deliberately uncomposed (recorded at angular-pigallery2-migration-record.ts:353); composing it is future work gated on the tiny-translator ownership decision. Capability counts moved 58->59 total / 50->51 experimental (crossProven stays 8); PM updated the two literal pins in packages/trust/test/. u10 capabilitiesExtracted accounting: 1 new (locale-id-provider) + 2 extended (workspace-script-flags i18n rows, template-i18n-runtime widened gate).
- T043-a ruling (2026-08-20): ingest journal seam is COMPLETE (four gates, per-field readFrom, declared-wins) - item (a) closes with no code change. The staged cache trees cannot pass gates 3/4 by construction (spike-staged, bespoke parity digests); minting offline journals is REJECTED as manufactured evidence. Unblock is consented re-acquire through acquire.ts (the shipped path), folded into T045 grind: acquire->run per candidate. T043 continues with item (c), the lockfile-foreign declared policy.
- OWNER DECISION PENDING (T044, brief complete 2026-08-20): authorize freeze supersession #2? Three measured frozen items (two ungated cell rewrites in angular-workspace-migration.ts + the families ETARGET table in angular-target-cell.ts). u1c proved the two gates necessary AND sufficient for a green angular2-hn build (5.3s, witness input observed). Without authorization: every Angular app terminates at build as defect:install/defect:build; the 13-cell investment stops at 7/9. Evidence: evidence/spikes/t046-angular-lane-build/ + T012-b2 run record. Second question (T043-b): may a proven row be reached through allow-foreign-lockfile while resolution drift is recorded but unenforced downstream?
- OWNER DECISION 3 (consent scope, from T045-b1, 2026-08-20): does VL-LEGACY-CORPUS-2026-08-10 reach non-MIT public OSS? Charter text says "public MIT source and dependencies"; the prior goal minted per-app grants (T680/T670/T685/T687) for jaeger-ui (Apache-2.0), saleor-dashboard (BSD-3), appsmith (Apache-2.0), strapi (split terms) - yet react-your-spotify (GPL-3.0) already sits in the corpus under the MIT-worded grant and acquire.ts applies no SPDX filter (an inconsistency to resolve, not paper over). No socket was opened for the four; the T045 react backlog holds until ruled: broaden the corpus consent, or mint per-app grants. Strapi stays excluded either way (SEE LICENSE IN LICENSE).
- Run restructure (orchestration, decided autonomously): Phase A+B under run id bank-demo-fleet-pipeline-p2b, Phase C+D under p2c, so no run crosses the 10-unit line mid-phase.

## Stop Rule

Stop only when a final audit proves both halves of the oracle. Do not stop after the pipeline is
automated — that is the enabler, not the outcome. Do not stop after one coverage batch while
apps remain cheap to admit.

Do not stop because a slice needs owner input, credentials, host capacity, or a policy decision.
Mark that exact slice blocked with a receipt, cut the smallest safe follow-up, and continue all
local work that still moves coverage.

## Slice Sizing

Safe means bounded, explicit, verified, and reversible — not tiny. A good Worker package here is
a whole pipeline stage folded into the command, a whole era cell, or a whole coverage batch. It
is not one helper, one contract file, or one doc note.

Coverage batches are explicitly *one* package each, not one Worker per app. Repeated same-shape
work goes in one package and is reviewed as a whole.

## Board Health

```bash
node /Users/jacksm5pro/.claude/skills/goal-prep/scripts/check-goal-state.mjs docs/goals/bank-demo-fleet-pipeline
```

## Canonical Board

`docs/goals/bank-demo-fleet-pipeline/state.yaml` — machine truth. If this charter disagrees,
`state.yaml` wins.

## Run Command

```text
/goal Follow docs/goals/bank-demo-fleet-pipeline/goal.md.
```

## PM Loop

1. Read this charter and `references/goal-execution.md` from the goal-prep skill.
2. Read `state.yaml`.
3. Re-check the intake, especially the likely misfire: is this turn building a demo or moving
   coverage?
4. Work only the active task; dispatch Worker packages through the fable-opus cockpit.
5. Write a compact receipt; update the board.
6. Advance to the next largest reversible package unless a phase, risk, rejected-verification,
   ambiguity, or completion boundary is due.
7. Finish only with an audit receipt mapping evidence to **both** oracle halves and recording

# One-Command Migration + Coverage Breadth

## Objective

Make `versionless migrate <app>` a single unattended command that runs from invocation to a
coverage report with **zero manual steps** — no hand-authored journeys, no per-app receipt
modules, no human opening files to check the migration worked — and then use that command to
grind as many additional real React and Angular apps through the pipeline as it will chew,
widening proven coverage so that when the owner runs it live on a top-10 US bank's own repo,
their apps largely just work.

Two things must become true, in this order, because the first is what makes the second
affordable:

1. **One command, end to end.** Today the full pipeline lives in fixture code and the operator
   `migrate` emits a non-installable tree (spike C). Every remaining manual stage —
   ingest, license-at-pin, era-cell provisioning, install/build, witness journey authoring,
   receipt module authoring — becomes a stage of one command that ends in a coverage report.
2. **Coverage breadth.** With authoring cost removed, run real React and Angular apps through
   that command continuously. Every app either raises proven coverage or emits a *named,
   countable, honest refusal* that becomes the next admission backlog item.

## Original Request

"use fable opus cockpit, goal prep, and 15m /loop to figure out where to continue versionless,
so that I can have it ready to show a large top 10 US bank and it being production ready for
doing a migration of older React and Angular apps"

Clarified by the owner during intake:

> "the actual demo to them will be when I do their repo. YOUR demos / equivalent will be more
> React and Angular apps to improve coverage as much as possible so that their apps transform
> would largely work. And it needs to be fully end to end where from command to done where it
> gives you the coverage report. We can't be having to expect someone manually check each file
> etc. part of the migration no, it should be as easy as versionless migrate or something"

## Intake Summary

- Input shape: `existing_plan` — the sealed owner decision brief
  (`docs/goals/next-tranche-strategy/notes/owner-decision-brief.md`) is a receipt-backed,
  audited plan. It is preserved as facts below and validated by T001 against the owner's
  clarified outcome, which it does not fully price.
- Audience: the owner (operator on stage), and downstream a top-10 US bank's migration team.
- Authority: `approved` — owner directed the tranche and named the sequencing constraint.
- Proof type: `demo` + `metric` — an unattended command run, and a coverage number that moves.
- Completion proof: a clean-checkout run of the single command against an app the pipeline has
  never handled, completing unattended to a coverage report, with a human-intervention count of
  zero; plus a strictly increased proven-app count and capability matrix versus the sealed
  baseline.
- Goal oracle: see below.
- Likely misfire: **building a beautiful staged demo instead of coverage.** The board could
  produce a polished one-command run over the existing fixture corpus, report success, and
  leave the bank's actual apps just as likely to fail. The command is the *enabler*; the
  coverage number is the product. A tranche that automates the pipeline and grinds no new apps
  has not met the outcome. The second misfire is **silent manual residue** — a stage that
  "works" because a human quietly does one step; T008 exists to catch exactly that.
- Blind spots considered:
  - "Zero manual steps" must be *measured*, not asserted. Hence an explicit intervention count.
  - Coverage breadth is bounded by admission, not by throughput (machine time is ~0.8 ms/app).
    Refusals, not slowness, are what cap the number — so refusals must be named and countable.
  - Honest-outcome vocabulary must survive automation: a synthesized journey that cannot reach
    a surface must still emit a bounded string, never a generic pass. Automation must not
    become a way to launder overclaim.
  - The bank's repo is unseen and unseeable in advance. The only defence is breadth plus
    legible refusal — an app that fails must fail with a named reason on stage, not a crash.
- Existing plan facts (preserved from the sealed brief, to validate not to obey):
  - Sealed baseline: 6/6 React + 4/4 Angular derived matrix; React holdout `passed` (76f0b5bd);
    Angular holdout `witness-passed-on-bounded-anonymous-catalog-surface` (fb921b46 — the
    bounded string is part of the claim); freeze `27741d9c`; three permanent REDs; 8
    capabilities cross-proven in-matrix, 50 experimental out.
  - Declared pre-Ivy boundary: "pre-Ivy-only dependencies (no published Ivy successor) in active
    application use ⇒ unsupported at the Angular 16 target cell" (observed 5-of-6, population
    statement). It stays true *for the 16 cell*; a 13 cell earns its own evidence.
  - Spike A: ngcc 12/13 feasible; honest cell **Angular 13.4.0 / Node 16**, real ngcc, rxjs 6.
    One library already Ivy, one back-compiles clean, one needs `-p module main`
    (exit-0-with-broken-typing trap documented). Est. ~25–35 units. Moves ~25 → ~125+ of the
    ~150-app Angular fleet.
  - Spike B: 0.8 ms/app median, whole fleet ~6s. Prune-after-receipt safe (offline verify passes
    with the work dir absent). Operator stages parallelizable; **witness must stay serialized**
    (determinism-under-load finding).
  - Spike C: unreached, not refuted — hit admission walls first. **Ejected-CRA / vendored-webpack
    trees are refused by the frozen adapter**; the operator `migrate` emits a non-installable
    tree; the full pipeline lives in fixture code.
  - Authoring is the cost: witness journeys/calibration were ~48% of the largest tranche's units.
    Journey synthesis from an app's own e2e suite is precedented (cypress-rwa holdout).
  - Carried tranche-two commitments: the ngcc 12/13 cell, and the format epoch (249 non-canonical
    files, 82 freeze-locked) riding the same freeze supersession (T003 ruling).
  - Host constraint: node-sass has no arm64 binding at any Node — era-cell runner pools need
    x64/Rosetta capacity.
  - Flagged one-liner: the fable-opus packet parser mishandles quote-wrapped contract bullets.

## Goal Oracle

The oracle for this goal is:

`In a clean checkout, a single command run against a real React or Angular application the
pipeline has never handled completes unattended — no human edits a file, authors a journey,
writes a receipt module, or inspects output to decide the result — and terminates in a coverage
report that either records the app as newly proven or names a countable refusal reason. Run
repeatedly, that command raises the proven-app count and capability matrix above the sealed
baseline.`

Two halves, both required. The command half is measured by a **human-intervention count of
zero** on an unseen app. The coverage half is measured by the **coverage report's own numbers**
moving against the sealed baseline, not by a description of progress.

The PM must keep comparing task receipts to this oracle. Automating a stage is not the oracle.
A green fixture run is not the oracle. Planning is not the oracle. The goal finishes only when a
final Judge/PM audit maps receipts and verification back to both halves and records
`full_outcome_complete: true`.

## Goal Kind

`existing_plan`

## Current Tranche

Continuous execution. Phase 1 closes every manual stage into one command and proves zero
intervention on an unseen app. Phase 2 opens admission (Angular 13 cell; ejected-CRA if the
census justifies it) and then grinds real apps through the command until the coverage report's
numbers stop moving cheaply or the owner calls the tranche.

Phase 1 carries no freeze motion. Phase 2's Angular 13 cell requires one authorized freeze
supersession, which the format epoch rides (one chain-touching epoch, not two).

## Non-Negotiable Constraints

- **Zero manual steps is the acceptance bar, and it is counted.** Any stage that still needs a
  human is either automated or explicitly recorded as an open intervention in the receipt. Do
  not describe a pipeline as end-to-end while a human step remains.
- **Automation must not launder overclaim.** Synthesized journeys inherit the same measured-pins
  and bounded-outcome vocabulary as hand-authored ones. An unreachable surface yields a bounded
  string, never a generic pass. Existing bounded claims are quoted verbatim, never restated more
  generally.
- **Refusals must be named and countable.** An app the pipeline cannot handle must exit with a
  specific admission string that a report can tally. A crash, a hang, or a non-installable tree
  is a defect, not a refusal.
- **Freeze discipline.** Phase 2's supersession is authorized, chain-recorded, single, and
  boundary amendments are append-only. The pre-Ivy boundary statement stays true for the 16 cell.
- **Witness stays serialized per host** (determinism-under-load finding). Operator stages may
  parallelize.
- **Prune-after-receipt is permitted** (proven safe); the evidence tree is the disk floor.
- Coverage claims stay derivation-guarded — the enterprise report and capability matrix remain
  offline-verifiable, and the payment/locality scans (`successfulNonLoopback: 0`) still gate.

## Execution Vehicle

Two dispatch systems are in play. Owner ruling (2026-08-17, after T004): **the fable-opus cockpit
is the Worker vehicle** — the original request named it and the PM's earlier reconciliation
(GoalBuddy agents by default) was reversed on owner instruction. Binding for this tranche:

- **Scout and Judge tasks stay on `goal-scout` / `goal-judge`.** They are read-only; the cockpit is
  a writer's harness and its scope guard has nothing to guard on a `- none` contract.
- **Unit sizing is bounded by the watchdog, not by task size.** The watchdog hook timeout in user
  settings is 2100s (35 min); a unit budget above that never alarms. Units are cut to finish in

run `npm run build` / `vp pack` unless the unit's own deliverable is regenerating the trust

# T012-b1 — Angular coverage batch, unit 1

Worker unit `bank-demo-fleet-pipeline-p2c/T012-b1-angular-batch`. 2026-08-20.
Board: `docs/goals/bank-demo-fleet-pipeline/state.yaml`. Discipline mirrored from
`notes/T027-react-batch-ruling.md`: a refusal is a returned outcome with a named code, and the
named code is the product. Proven bar per T028: all nine stages `ran` **and** `interventionCount 0`.

The `angular-13.4.0` cell became plannable at supersession commit `e9a626d`
(composite `140ce86e`). This unit is the first coverage evidence spent against it.

---

## 1. Enumeration (recorded before any run)

What the batch infrastructure already knows, read off disk on 2026-08-20:

- **Batch manifests already written:** `evidence/runs/fleet-batch/t013a-react-fleet.json`,
  `evidence/runs/fleet-batch/t029-react-fleet.json`. Both are React fleets. **No Angular
  manifest existed** before this unit; this unit writes
  `evidence/runs/fleet-batch/t012b1-angular-fleet.json`.
- **Acquired corpus:** `.versionless/cache/` (84 entries) and `.versionless/work/` (39 lanes).
  Consent for any acquire: `VL-LEGACY-CORPUS-2026-08-10`. **No acquire was performed by this
  unit** — every candidate below is a tree already on disk, or is recorded as not attemptable
  because its tree is not on disk.
- **Coverage report before this unit** (`evidence/trust/current/coverage-report.json` totals):
  `{applications: 21, proven: 11, bounded: 2, refused: 5, not-admitted: 3}`.
  Angular rows: 4 proven (`angular-factoriolab`, `angular-jira-clone`,
  `angular-tiny-translator-v0-12-0`, `angular-super-productivity-v2-13-15`), 1 bounded
  (`holdout-angular-eshop-webspa`), 1 not-admitted (`angular-realworld-v15-to-v16`).
  That is the 4/4 Angular matrix line the guards say may only grow.
- **Refusal census before this unit:** 192 sites, `adapterFreezeComposite 140ce86e…`. The census
  counts refusal *sites in source*, not applications, so a coverage batch that edits no source
  cannot move it — and this unit edits no source.

### Angular candidates, with era

Era rule applied: **AngularJS-era (1.x) applications are NOT candidates**; Angular-CLI-era
(2+) applications are. Cell rule applied: an application whose own era is below the Ivy line
(pre-13) is declared against `--cell angular-13.4.0`; anything modern-era lets the default 16
path stand.

| candidate | era read from disk | tree on disk | candidate? | cell declared |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `angular2-hn` | `@angular/core ~9.0.1`, `@angular/cli ~9.0.2` — Angular-CLI era, pre-Ivy-default | `.versionless/cache/angular2-hn/acquisition/source` (full tree, `yarn.lock` only, no `package-lock.json`) | **yes** | `angular-13.4.0` |
| `angular-kubernetes-dashboard` (`…-stage-t678`) | `@angular/core 12.2.9`, `@angular/cli 12.2.9`, `engines.node >=14.16.1`, `engines.npm >=6 <7` | `.versionless/cache/angular-kubernetes-dashboard-stage-t678/acquisition/source` (full tree, `package-lock.json` present) | **yes** | `angular-13.4.0` |
| `angular-kubernetes-dashboard-stage-t674` | — | `acquisition/source` exists but holds **0 files** | no — nothing to run | n/a |
| `angular-kubernetes-dashboard-stage-t676` | — | `acquisition/source` holds **0 files** | no — nothing to run | n/a |
| `angular-openmf-web-app-stage-t672` | — | `acquisition/source` holds **0 files** | no — nothing to run | n/a |
| `angular-openmf-web-app-stage-t673` | — | `acquisition/source` holds **0 files** | no — nothing to run | n/a |
| `angular-fuxa` | Angular-CLI era | **no extracted tree.** `.versionless/cache/tier-f/angular-fuxa/4913aabf…/source.tar.gz` is a tarball; `fixtures/angular-fuxa/` carries only `fixture.json`, `journey.json`, `provenance.json`, `technical-evaluation-policy.json`; `.versionless/cache/angular-fuxa-production/3b439473…` is a dependency closure cache (npm-cache + tarballs), not sources | **candidate, not attemptable as-is** | n/a |
| `angular-phonecat`, `angular-phonecat-vite8` | **AngularJS 1.x** | present | **no** — excluded by era rule | n/a |
| `angular-eshop-webspa-netcore2-2-*` | Angular-CLI era | present | no — already the sealed **bounded** holdout `holdout-angular-eshop-webspa` | n/a |
| `angular-pigallery2-v1-7-0-*` | Angular-CLI era | present | no — already the sealed holdout `holdout-angular-pigallery2` | n/a |
| `angular-factoriolab-*`, `angular-jira-clone-*`, `angular-tiny-translator-v0-12-0-*`, `angular-super-productivity-v2-13-15-*` | Angular-CLI era | present | no — already **proven** in the coverage report; re-running buys no coverage delta | n/a |
| `angular-realworld-v15`, `angular-realworld-v16` | Angular-CLI era | **closure caches only**, no source tree | no — already the **not-admitted** row `angular-realworld-v15-to-v16` | n/a |
| `angular-13-cell-runtime`, `harness-angular-realworld-fonts` | — | present | no — these are the era-cell Node runtime and a witness font cache, not applications | n/a |

**Attemptable this unit: 2** (`angular2-hn`, `angular-kubernetes-dashboard`).
Both are pre-Ivy-era, so both are declared against the newly published `angular-13.4.0` cell;
no candidate in this unit's enumeration lets the default 16 path stand.

Ordered smallest-first, as the packet's budget rule requires: `angular2-hn` (a small
single-app tree) before `angular-kubernetes-dashboard` (a large multi-language monorepo whose
frontend closure is the heaviest install in the enumeration).

---

## 2. Batch invocation

Mirrors the T021/T029/T030 sequencing exactly — `--publish` ordering, the three fleet-wide
install policies forwarded, lane root outside the repository, one application at a time.
`VERSIONLESS_NETWORK_MODE=offline` is **not** set on the batch (standing rule: install must
reach the registry; only the publish steps are offline, and the batch sets that itself).

```
node --experimental-strip-types packages/cli/src/cli.ts batch \
  --apps evidence/runs/fleet-batch/t012b1-angular-fleet.json \
  --out <scratchpad>/t012b1 \
  --name t012b1-angular-13cell \
  --cell angular-13.4.0 \
  --allow-remote-tarballs --allow-install-scripts --allow-peer-conflicts \
  --publish --json
```

`--cell` is a forwarded era-cell value flag on `batch`
(`packages/cli/src/operator/flows.ts:150`, `ERA_CELL_VALUE_FLAGS`), and `batch` forwards it to
every application's harness unchanged. It is therefore a **per-batch**, not a per-application,
declaration — which is why the 13-cell candidates are cut as their own batch. This unit's
enumeration produced no default-16 candidate, so no second batch was needed.

---

### 2.1 A second batch was required, and why

The first batch (`t012b1-angular-13cell`, both applications) refused **both** at stage 2 with
`ingest.revision-not-determined`:

> Ingest: `<root>` carries no readable Git metadata and no acquisition journal of this pipeline's
> own names it, so the revision this source is pinned to is not something this stage read. An
> unpinned source has no revision for the licence reading or any later record to be relative to;
> declare it with `--revision <commit-sha>`.

That is correct behaviour, not a defect: these two trees are **staged corpus extractions**, not
`.versionless/work/<id>/baseline` acquisition lanes, so `acquisitionLaneOf` finds nothing and no
`evidence/ingests/<id>/source.json` names them. The refusal names its own remedy, and the
remedy's value is **read off disk, never guessed**:

- `angular2-hn` → `f6cc578d66c6fa7997f6ef46c7ed4488a85002d8`, read from
  `.versionless/cache/angular2-hn/acquisition/downloads/commit.json` and confirmed by the
  archive filename `angular2-hn-f6cc578d….tar.gz` in the same directory.
- `angular-kubernetes-dashboard` → `e75ebcf688d3b7edff2a050332c8e86ca1e47e12`, read from the
  accepted-response ledger in `evidence/ingests/angular-kubernetes-dashboard/t678/terminal.json`
  (`https://codeload.github.com/kubernetes-retired/dashboard/tar.gz/e75ebcf6…`, sha256
  `c8b637c000b40c…`), **verified** against the tree on disk:
  `shasum -a 256 .versionless/cache/angular-kubernetes-dashboard-stage-t678/acquisition/source.tar.gz`
  = `c8b637c000b40c2cefff3bb27723451732161505ca4f77bb86dfbb9e33a24923`, identical.

`--revision` is a per-application declaration that `batch` forwards to every application
unchanged, so two applications with two revisions cannot share one batch. The second batch
therefore carries `angular2-hn` alone.

---

## 3. Per-application outcomes

### `angular2-hn` — **refused: `install.lockfile-foreign`** (6 of 9 stages ran)

Batch `t012b1-angular2-hn-13cell`, `--cell angular-13.4.0`,
`--revision f6cc578d66c6fa7997f6ef46c7ed4488a85002d8`, 1027 ms, **interventionCount 0**.

| stage | status |
|---|---|
| analyze | `ran` |
| ingest | `ran` |
| license-at-pin | `ran` |
| era-cell | `ran` |
| plan | `ran` |
| apply | `ran` |
| install | **`refused`** |
| build | `not-run` |
| witness | `not-run` |

Not proven: the T028 bar needs all nine `ran`, and three did not run. Refusal verbatim:

> Install: the lane carries yarn.lock, and this stage reads package-lock.json,
> npm-shrinkwrap.json. The closure is pinned — by yarn — and it is pinned in a lockfile this flow
> does not read, so it is not absent and it is not installable here.

**This is the first coverage evidence bought with the `angular-13.4.0` cell, and it is
affirmative.** The era-cell row records `cell: "angular-13.4.0"`, `cellSource: "declared"`,
`cellBasis: "published by the frozen Angular adapter as an AngularTargetCell; the Node line is
the cell's own nodeLine declaration"`, runtime `16.20.2` read from `angular-13.4.0#nodeLine`. An
Angular **9.0.1** application the pipeline had never seen was admitted by the 13 cell, planned
and applied, and got as far as the install gate. Before the supersession this application had no
plannable target cell at all. What stops it is a package-manager gate, not an Angular one.

Backlog item this names: **`install.lockfile-foreign` is now the top Angular admission wall.**
It is a yarn-vs-npm reading, entirely orthogonal to Angular era, and it is already the top React
wall too (`t030-fleet-install-policies`: 2 of 6 rows). A yarn-lockfile reader would move this
application off the wall without touching the adapter.

### `angular-kubernetes-dashboard` — **refused: `ingest.revision-not-determined`** (1 of 9 stages ran)

Batch `t012b1-angular-13cell`, `--cell angular-13.4.0`, 1380 ms, **interventionCount 0**.
`analyze` ran; `ingest` refused; the remaining seven are `not-run`.

This row is **not a reading of the application** — it is the pipeline declining a tree whose
revision was not declared on the command line. The revision has since been read and verified
(§2.1) but the re-run did not fit this unit's wall clock (see §4), so the standing row in the
coverage report is the stage-2 refusal. The next unit re-runs it with
`--revision e75ebcf688d3b7edff2a050332c8e86ca1e47e12` and that row is expected to move.

Carried honestly for whoever picks it up: a prior task already filed a **terminal failure** for
this application at its own historical-qualification stage —
`evidence/ingests/angular-kubernetes-dashboard/t678/terminal.json`, property
`loopback-api-contract`, "Kubernetes Dashboard loopback Kubernetes API source contract is
absent". That is a witness-reachability finding, not an admission finding; it does not stop the
first eight stages, but it predicts a bounded rather than a proven outcome at the witness.

### Not attempted this unit

| candidate | why |
|---|---|
| `angular-kubernetes-dashboard` (re-run with `--revision`) | wall clock. Its `package-lock.json` closure is the heaviest install in the enumeration and the unit's 35 minutes were spent on enumeration, the two batches, and this record. Revision read and verified; the next unit runs it first. |
| `angular-fuxa` | no extracted tree. Its bytes exist only as `.versionless/cache/tier-f/angular-fuxa/4913aabf…/source.tar.gz`. Extracting a tarball into a lane by hand is not something this packet authorises, and the acquire that would do it properly needs a repository/ref decision this unit did not have. Cheap for a follow-up unit that is cut to make that decision. |
| `angular-kubernetes-dashboard-stage-t674` / `-t676`, `angular-openmf-web-app-stage-t672` / `-t673` | `acquisition/source` holds **0 files** on disk. Nothing to run; these are staging shells, not trees. An acquire under `VL-LEGACY-CORPUS-2026-08-10` would be needed to give openmf-web-app a tree at all. |

---

## 4. Budget

35 minutes declared. Enumeration and the read of `batch.ts` / T027 / the charter took the first
third; the two batches took ~3 seconds of machine time between them; the rest is this record.
Nothing was guessed to fit the budget, and every unstarted candidate is named above with the
reason it is unstarted.

---

## 5. Coverage delta

```
  --apps evidence/runs/fleet-batch/t012b1-angular-fleet.json \
  --out <scratchpad>/t012b1 \
  --name t012b1-angular-13cell \
  --cell angular-13.4.0 \
  --allow-remote-tarballs --allow-install-scripts --allow-peer-conflicts \
  --publish --json
```

`--cell` is a forwarded era-cell value flag on `batch`
(`packages/cli/src/operator/flows.ts:150`, `ERA_CELL_VALUE_FLAGS`), and `batch` forwards it to
every application's harness unchanged. It is therefore a **per-batch**, not a per-application,
declaration — which is why the 13-cell candidates are cut as their own batch. This unit's
enumeration produced no default-16 candidate, so no second batch was needed.

---

The first batch (`t012b1-angular-13cell`, both applications) refused **both** at stage 2 with
`ingest.revision-not-determined`:

> own names it, so the revision this source is pinned to is not something this stage read. An
> unpinned source has no revision for the licence reading or any later record to be relative to;
> declare it with `--revision <commit-sha>`.

That is correct behaviour, not a defect: these two trees are **staged corpus extractions**, not
`.versionless/work/<id>/baseline` acquisition lanes, so `acquisitionLaneOf` finds nothing and no
`evidence/ingests/<id>/source.json` names them. The refusal names its own remedy, and the
remedy's value is **read off disk, never guessed**:

unchanged, so two applications with two revisions cannot share one batch. The second batch
therefore carries `angular2-hn` alone.

### 14.2 `react-verdaccio-v4-12-2` — acquire **source-bound**, run **refused: `ingest.frontend-root-declares-no-framework`** (1 of 9 stages ran), interventionCount 0

The acquire went through cleanly and is the first thing in this repository to prove the
generic path end to end on a repository it had no module for:

```
VERSIONLESS_NETWORK_MODE=consented node --experimental-strip-types packages/cli/src/cli.ts \
  acquire verdaccio/verdaccio --ref v4.12.2 --id react-verdaccio-v4-12-2 \
  --consent VL-LEGACY-CORPUS-2026-08-10 --json
```

`result: source-bound`, 7 requests, 3.1 s wall. `refs/tags/v4.12.2` resolved as an **annotated**
tag `48c9f8bc…` dated `2021-06-23T17:16:55Z` onto commit `4fd08e63557d6bfd0e1183b60e8bc4c3a9f14bff`
— **the same commit the T682 journal recorded**, so the pin the old goal fetched and the pin the
shipped path resolves are the same object. Archive parity: `missingFiles 0, extraFiles 0,
mismatchedBlobs 0` over 525 git blobs / 751 safe entries, single root
`verdaccio-4fd08e63557d6bfd0e1183b60e8bc4c3a9f14bff`. Licence read at the pin:
`identifier MIT`, `identifierSource observed`, `Copyright (c) 2018 Verdaccio community`.
Record at `evidence/ingests/react-verdaccio-v4-12-2/source.json`, attempt
`25537a2e…`, baseline at `.versionless/work/react-verdaccio-v4-12-2/baseline`.

The run then stopped at ingest, verbatim:

> Ingest: none of the directories considered declares react, next or angular, so this stage read
> no frontend to admit: `.` declares no framework this stage reads. A directory carrying a
> manifest is not a frontend; declare the one that is with `--frontend-root <dir>`.

**No `--frontend-root` was declared, because there is none to declare.** Verdaccio 4.12.2 does
not carry its React UI in this tree: the root manifest declares zero `react` dependency (only
`eslint-plugin-react` and `eslint-plugin-react-hooks` as devDependencies), and every other
`package.json` under the pin that mentions `react` is a fixture inside `test/` or
`docker-examples/`. The UI ships from a separate package at this era. The refusal is therefore
**terminal and correct**: the pipeline was pointed at a Node registry server and said so.

The analyze row that did run is still worth the ink: `packageManager {manager: yarn, lockfiles: [yarn.lock]}`,
`nodeEra {declared: "13", source: ".nvmrc"}`, and 112 dependencies all `unknown` to the cell —
"The frozen React and Next.js adapters publish no target-cell package registry, so no per-package
verdict exists for this lineage."

**Finding: `react-verdaccio` was mis-enumerated as a react candidate.** It is not one at this pin.
The T682 staging tree on disk has always been a Node server. That is not a pipeline wall — it is
the pipeline correctly declining to invent a frontend, at intervention count 0, in 0.3 s.

### 14.3 `react-coverview-a1470b01` — **PROVEN**, 9 of 9 stages ran, interventionCount 0

The one the packet said could reach proven today, and it did.

Prior record (T029 batch): `defect` at `install`, exit 1 — "the declared policies were applied and
the pinned closure still did not install", `npm install … --legacy-peer-deps` failing on a
git-protocol dependency the batch had no policy for. That record is preserved, renamed to
`evidence/runs/react-coverview-a1470b01/t029-install-defect-run-record.json` (+ `.interventions.json`)
per the u6 pattern; nothing was deleted or rewritten.

Re-run with `--allow-git-dependencies` declared alongside the other four:

- `outcome: proceeded`, `exitCode 0`
- `analyze:ran ingest:ran license-at-pin:ran era-cell:ran plan:ran apply:ran install:ran build:ran witness:ran`
- `interventionCount 0`, `invocations 1`, `stdinReads 0`, `mutatedPathsOutsideWriteSet []`, `authoringPathsTouched []`
- `terminalClassification: "proven"`
- roots: `frontendBasis: ". declares react ^16.14.0 (dependencies.react)"` — the application root is its own frontend root
- coverage row: `{status: "proven", provenanceOfStatus: "run-record", interventionCount: 0, source: {repository: "rutikwankhade/CoverView", ref/revision: "a1470b01e41c9e1128364e500b2ca2107f8432e0", license: "MIT"}}`

**T028 bar met exactly: 9/9 `ran` and count 0.** This is the second application ever admitted to
proven by run-record derivation, and the first one the `git-dependencies` policy bought.
`react-flame-v2-4-0` was the template; this is the template applied to an application the
policy work of T043-b was aimed at.

### 14.4 `react-antd-admin-template-v2-0-0` — **refused: `install.closure-registry-unreachable`** (6 of 9 stages ran), interventionCount 0

Prior record (T029 batch) was a **defect** at install, exit 1 — npm failed and the flow had no
name for why. Preserved as `t029-install-defect-run-record.json` (+ `.interventions.json`).

Re-run with the same five policies: `outcome: refused`, exit 2,
`analyze:ran ingest:ran license-at-pin:ran era-cell:ran plan:ran apply:ran install:refused
build:not-run witness:not-run`, `interventionCount 0`. The refusal, verbatim:

> Install: this closure pins `registry.npm.taobao.org`, and npm could not reach it —
> `CERT_HAS_EXPIRED`, requesting `https://registry.npm.taobao.org/word-wrap/download/word-wrap-1.2.3.tgz`.
> There is no policy to declare here and this flow offers none: no allowance makes an unreachable
> registry answer, and a closure that resolves through a registry that is gone cannot be installed
> as recorded. What this establishes is that this run did not reach `registry.npm.taobao.org`;
> whether that host is retired or momentarily unreachable is not established here, and neither is
> what it would have served. The remedy is re-pinning the closure onto a registry that answers,
> which changes what the application declares and is therefore a migration decision rather than an
> install policy.

**This is the honesty motion the packet predicted, measured.** The same application, the same
pinned closure, the same host: what was an unnamed `defect` is now a named `refused` with the
non-claim attached ("whether that host is retired … is not established here"). A defect says the
pipeline broke; a refusal says the world did. The second is true here, and the flow now says so.

### 14.5 Not attempted this unit — **consent scope**, and why that is the honest answer

Four of the five priority-1 staged apps were **not acquired**. The reason is not budget and not a
pipeline wall: it is that the charter's consent grant names one licence.

> "Use purpose-bound consent ID `VL-LEGACY-CORPUS-2026-08-10` for acquisition of public **MIT**
> source and dependencies." — `docs/goals/legacy-react-angular-production-readiness/goal.md`,
> restated in `docs/goals/next-tranche-strategy/goal.md` as "for any public MIT acquisition".

`jaeger-ui` and `appsmith` are Apache-2.0, `saleor-dashboard` is BSD-3-Clause, and `strapi` v3.6.8
declares `SEE LICENSE IN LICENSE` over a root `LICENSE` that opens "Portions of the Strapi software
are licensed as follows" — a split-terms file, the least clear of the four. None is MIT.

Two facts point in opposite directions and both are recorded rather than resolved here:

1. **Against the strict reading:** `react-your-spotify-1-5-0` is already in this corpus, acquired
   under `VL-LEGACY-CORPUS-2026-08-10`, with `licence.identifier: "GPL-3.0"` — so a non-MIT source
   has been fetched under this grant before, and `acquire.ts` itself applies no SPDX filter (its
   licence gate is a presence-and-identification check, per its own header).
2. **For the strict reading:** every one of these four was originally acquired under its **own**
   purpose-bound consent — `T680-jaeger-ui-production-acquisition`,
   `T670-saleor-dashboard-production-acquisition`, `T685-appsmith-v1.5.9-production-acquisition`,
   `T687-strapi-v3.6.8-production-acquisition`. The previous goal minted a separate grant per
   non-MIT application, which is exactly what one does when the corpus grant does not reach.

The standing rule is "do NOT acquire on an uncertain consent", and fact 2 is a strong signal that
the corpus grant was never meant to reach these. So: **no socket was opened for any of the four.**
They are recorded as `not-attempted-this-unit: consent-scope-unresolved`, and the question is
escalated to the owner rather than decided by a worker. This costs four candidates and buys the
one thing a consent record is for.

Nothing about these four's *pipeline* outcome is established by this unit. Their trees are still on
disk under `.versionless/cache/<stage-id>/acquisition/source`; what is missing is a journal the four
ingest gates accept, and the only shipped way to produce one is `acquire`.

### 14.6 Angular candidate — not attempted this unit

Priority 3 was budget-conditional and the budget went to publishing a verified surface instead.
Nothing new is claimed or denied about the Angular lane: §13.6's two owner-gated cell-gates remain
exactly where T046-u6 left them, and the `angular: 4 counted of 4` matrix line is verbatim.

### 14.7 Coverage delta

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `applications` | 23 | **24** |
| `proven` | 11 | **12** |
| `bounded` | 2 | 2 |
| `refused` | 5 | **7** |
| `not-admitted` | 5 | **3** |

Reconciled row by row, so the arithmetic is not a coincidence:

- `react-coverview-a1470b01`: `not-admitted` → **`proven`** (+1 proven, −1 not-admitted)
- `react-antd-admin-template-v2-0-0`: `not-admitted` → **`refused`** (+1 refused, −1 not-admitted)
- `react-verdaccio-v4-12-2`: **new** application, `refused` (+1 application, +1 refused)

Two of the three moves are honesty motions rather than capability motions — a defect that became a
named refusal, and a new row that refused. The third is real coverage: **proven 11 → 12**, and the
floor the guards hold at 11 grew rather than moved.

**Guards, all checked after publishing:**

- `react: 6 counted of 6 proven cells` — unchanged; a run-record proof is not a Judge-counted cell,
  and the report still says so in its own `notEstablished`.
- `angular: 4 counted of 4 proven cells` — verbatim.
- `adapter-freeze.json` composite `140ce86e…` — unmoved; no source changed.
- `evidence/runs/react-flame-v2-4-0` and `evidence/runs/angular2-hn` — byte-identical to `HEAD`.
- `git diff HEAD -- packages` — empty.

### 14.8 Publish state

Batch ordering, run after the last record landed:

- `trust:generate --offline --policy trust/policy.json --output evidence/trust/current` — regenerated,
  canonical digest `77b8e46c00a9dd2e…`, deterministic core `31e7de863bf7b2df…`, 12 artifacts.
  (Note for the runbook: `trust:generate` requires **both** `--offline` **and**
  `VERSIONLESS_NETWORK_MODE=offline`, and it requires `--policy` and `--output` explicitly — the
  bare `npm run trust:generate -- --offline` in §1 of the runbook is not a runnable line.)
- `trust:verify --offline` — `valid: true`, digest `77b8e46c00a9dd2e…`, 12 artifacts.
- `report:coverage --offline --verify-only` — `pass`, coverage digest `61b5e20a76d2b040…`,
  machine artifact `532081b7…`, human document `ce8241a3…`.
- `receipt:verify` — `valid: true`, 10 artifacts.
- `corpus:verify` (offline) — `pass`, 20 verticals, 14 source applications.
- `refusal-census --verify-only` — `matchesPublished: true`, **198 sites, unmoved**. No source
  changed, so no site moved; the census was verified rather than regenerated.

### 14.9 Findings for a properly-cut unit (no source was changed here)

1. **`--allow-git-dependencies` is worth a proven row on its own.** T043-b built the policy;
   this unit is the first evidence that it converts a real application from `defect` to `proven`
   with nothing else changed. The T029 batch's coverview failure was never a pipeline defect —
   it was a missing policy, and the record now says which one.
2. **A defect that becomes a named refusal is a coverage motion even though the numerator does
   not move.** antd-admin sits at exactly the same wall it did in T029; what changed is that the
   wall now has a name, a non-claim, and a stated remedy that is honestly labelled a *migration*
   decision rather than an install policy. The `not-admitted → refused` transition is the
   measurable form of that, and this unit is the first to record one.
3. **Enumeration by ecosystem reputation is not enumeration by pin.** `react-verdaccio` was
   carried as a react candidate through five task numbers. At its pin it declares no react
   dependency at all. One `analyze` row, 0.3 s, settled it. Any future candidate list should be
   screened by reading the manifest at the pin — the pipeline will do it for free and refuse
   honestly, but a candidate that costs an acquire to disqualify is a candidate that could have
   been disqualified from the journal already on disk.
4. **The corpus consent's scope is the binding constraint on T045's remaining backlog, not the
   pipeline.** Four of the five priority-1 candidates are blocked on a licence question a worker
   must not decide. Until it is settled, the acquire→run grind's react backlog is materially
   smaller than the candidate list suggests, and the next unit should be cut against MIT sources
   or against an owner ruling — not against this list again.

# T045 candidate screen — read the manifest at the pin before spending anything

Worker unit `bank-demo-fleet-pipeline-p2f/T045-b2-candidate-rescreen`. 2026-08-20.
**Read-only.** No socket was opened, no `acquire` was run, `VERSIONLESS_NETWORK_MODE` was never
set, and nothing outside this one file was written. Every reading below came off disk: staged
corpus trees, acquisition lanes, tier-F source tarballs (read to stdout, never extracted), the
old goals' ingest journals, and `evidence/trust/current/coverage-report.json`.

## 0. Why this unit exists

T045-b1 §14.9 finding 3, verbatim:

> **Enumeration by ecosystem reputation is not enumeration by pin.** `react-verdaccio` was
> carried as a react candidate through five task numbers. At its pin it declares no react
> dependency at all. One `analyze` row, 0.3 s, settled it.

It cost a consented acquire (7 requests, 3.1 s, 55 MB of registry server) to learn something the
staged `package.json` already on disk had been saying since T682. This screen reads every
remaining candidate's manifest **at its pin**, offline, before any further acquire spend or
consent request is made against it.

The screen is exact rather than impressionistic: it replays the shipped frontend-root reading
(`packages/cli/src/operator/ingest.ts:465-600` — root plus immediate subdirectories only, each
read for `@angular/core` → `next` → `react` over `dependencies` merged with `devDependencies`)
and the shipped React admission rule (`packages/cli/src/operator/plan.ts:355` keys on the exact
`react-scripts` key; `:392` on a `vite.config.{ts,js,mjs}` file; anything else refuses
`plan.react.no-frozen-adapter-claims-this-tree`). Predicted walls are therefore derived from the
code that will judge these trees, not guessed.

---

## 1. The candidate universe, and where each name came from

Enumerated from: the T045 card (`state.yaml:2787`), `notes/T012-angular-batch.md` §1 and §14,
`evidence/ingests/**` (66 directories), `evidence/runs/**` not-attempted and refused rows, the
published coverage report's 24 rows, and the two prior goals
(`docs/goals/legacy-react-angular-production-readiness/`,
`docs/goals/react-angular-migration-spine/`) where their dispositions are referenced.

Names that carry no tree and no candidacy are disposed of first, so the working list is honest:

| name | disposition | evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `react-verdaccio-stage-t681`, `react-unleash-stage-t686`, `react-kafka-ui-v0-3-3-stage-t690`, `react-mattermost-stage-t688`, `react-apisix-dashboard-stage-t684`, `react-sqlpad-v5-5-0-closure-stage`, `angular-kubernetes-dashboard-stage-t674`/`-t676`, `angular-openmf-web-app-stage-t672`/`-t673` | **no tree** — `acquisition/source` holds 0 files (apisix/mattermost/kafka-ui hold only ledger and archive fragments) | their `terminal.json` all stopped before or during transport: unleash `getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND registry.npmjs.org`; mattermost and kafka-ui `non-200-status` 404; apisix `durable-response-ledger-after-gpg-import-hang`; openmf t672 `getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND api.github.com`, t673 "openMF official repository identity or rights differs"; k8s t674/t676 transport |
| `react-netlify-cms`, `react-redux-realworld`, `react-shlink-web-client` | **terminally excluded by the prior goal**, must not be recycled | `legacy-react-angular-production-readiness/state.yaml:127`: "Netlify CMS is terminally excluded; React Redux RealWorld T710 failed its derived-asset plan; Shlink T714 is permanently excluded. These cannot be silently recycled as candidates." `react-shlink-web-client/t714/terminal.json` `result: "permanent-exclusion"` |
| `react-calculator`, `react-excalidraw-v011`, `react-graphiql-013`, `react-graphql-playground`, `react-openchakra`, `react-parse-dashboard`, `react-phoenix-trello`, `react-quiz-app`, `react-shopping-cart`, `react-sound-redux`, `react-takenote`, `react-tetris`, `react-winds`, `react-actual-budget-v22-12-9`, `react-taskcafe-v032` | **consumed-failed / terminal-exclusion journals only, no tree** | e.g. `react-taskcafe-v032/terminal.json` `reason: "required-release-and-ref-not-found"`; the rest carry `consumed-failed.json` or `t5xx-exclusion.json` and no `acquisition/source` |
| `react-answer-v2-0-2`, `react-casdoor-v3-154-3`, `react-emoji-search-style-import` | **0-byte ingest directories and 0-file caches** | `evidence/ingests/<id>` is 0 B; `.versionless/cache/<id>-source` is 0 B |
| `angular-phonecat`, `angular-phonecat-vite8` | **not candidates** — AngularJS 1.x, excluded by T012's era rule | T012 §1 |
| `angular-realworld-v15-to-v16` | already a published `not-admitted` row, Judge-declined | coverage row: "the migration changed applicationFilesChanged=0 application files … excluded from the Angular denominator" |
| `angular-13-cell-runtime`, `harness-angular-realworld-fonts`, `react-mycrypto-pm`, `pnpm-*`, `xdg-cache`, `trust` | not applications | T012 §1 |
| the 12 proven + 2 bounded coverage rows | re-running buys no coverage delta | coverage report |

That leaves **sixteen live candidates**, screened one by one below.

---

## 2. The screen, candidate by candidate

Framework readings are the exact string the ingest stage will record. Licences are quoted from
the manifest field and/or the root `LICENSE` blob at the pin.

### 2.1 `react-cra-redux-1a06509b` — RUNNABLE-NOW

- Tree: `.versionless/work/react-cra-redux-1a06509b/baseline` (acquisition lane, journal already
  passed all four ingest gates on 2026-08-17). **440 K, 21 files, 12 declared dependencies.**
- Framework: `. declares react 16.14.0 (dependencies.react)`.
- Bundler origin: `react-scripts 2.1.8`, `public/index.html` present → the frozen create-react-app
  adapter claims it (`plan.ts:355`).
- Licence: manifest carries **no `license` field** (`private: true`); root `LICENSE` reads
  "MIT License / Copyright (c) 2017 Jamie Barton".
- Consent: **none needed** — the baseline is already in the corpus and the run spends no socket.
- Published row: `refused`, `install.lockfile-foreign`, `interventionCount 0`.
- **Predicted next wall: witness.** The row's refusal was recorded 2026-08-17; the
  `--allow-foreign-lockfile` policy that answers it did not exist until T043-b landed on
  2026-08-20. Its only lockfile is `yarn.lock`. With the five-policy declaration T045-b1 already
  uses, install has an answer, and nothing between install and witness is predicted to refuse.

### 2.2 `react-your-spotify-1-5-0` — RUNNABLE-NOW

- Tree: `.versionless/work/react-your-spotify-1-5-0/baseline`. **2.6 M, 423 files**; frontend
  `client/` declares 38 dependencies.
- Framework: `client declares react ^18.2.0 (dependencies.react)`; `server declares no framework
  this stage reads` — exactly one declaring directory, so `frontendRoot` **reads** as `client`
  with no declaration needed.
- Bundler origin: `react-scripts ^5.0.1`, `client/public/index.html` present → CRA adapter claims it.
- Licence: **GPL-3.0** — root `LICENSE` opens "GNU GENERAL PUBLIC LICENSE / Version 3, 29 June 2007";
  `evidence/ingests/react-your-spotify-1-5-0/source.json` records `licence.identifier "GPL-3.0"`
  under consent `VL-LEGACY-CORPUS-2026-08-10`.
- Consent: **none needed for the run.** The acquire already happened; this unit raises no new
  consent question by re-running an application already in the corpus. (Its *presence* is one of
  the two facts owner decision 3 must reconcile — see §5.)
- Published row: `refused`, `install.lockfile-foreign`, recorded 2026-08-17, same pre-policy vintage.
- **Predicted next wall: witness.**

### 2.3 `angular-contacts` — RUNNABLE-AFTER-T044 (cheapest Angular candidate on disk)

- Tree: tier-F tarball only —
  `.versionless/cache/tier-f/angular-contacts/93b2add6…/source.tar.gz`, **168 K**, root
  `angular-contacts-app-example-875aa2df7f5f87b6731a1259b63e2b399fa5fb3f/`. Repository
  `aslanvatsaev/angular-contacts-app-example` @ `875aa2df7f5f87b6731a1259b63e2b399fa5fb3f`
  (`evidence/ingests/angular-contacts/t092-ingest.json`).
- Framework: `. declares angular 9.0.0 (dependencies.@angular/core)`; `@angular/cli ^9.0.1`;
  `scripts.build: "ng build"`; `angular.json` present.
- Lockfile: **`package-lock.json`** — npm, so no `lockfile-foreign` wall.
- Licence: manifest has no `license` field (`private: true`); root `LICENSE` reads
  "MIT License / Copyright (c) 2019 Aslan Vatsaev". **MIT.**

**Two candidates are runnable right now at zero cost** — no socket, no consent, no declaration. `react-cra-redux-1a06509b` (440 K, 12 deps) and `react-your-spotify-1-5-0` (2.6 M, client reads without `--frontend-root`) both carry a published `refused` row with code `install.lockfile-foreign`, recorded 2026-08-17 — three days *before* `--allow-foreign-lockfile` shipped in T043-b. That is the next batch unit's entire opening.

**The consent backlog is smaller and differently shaped than the ruling assumes.** `saleor-dashboard` looked strongest on its manifest — single root, `react ^16.12.0`, npm `package-lock.json` — but it declares neither `react-scripts` nor `vite`; it declares `webpack ^4.35.3` with its own `webpack.config.js`, so the consent would buy `plan.react.no-frozen-adapter-claims-this-tree`, not a proven row. `strapi` needs no ruling at all: T596 already excluded it canonically, and `packages/strapi-admin/ee/LICENSE` is on disk. Meanwhile `angular-kubernetes-dashboard` is Apache-2.0 and its T043-a-mandated re-acquire path is consent-blocked in exactly the same way — which the ruling does not currently list.

**A third consent precedent nobody had recorded.** `evidence/ingests/angular-ionic-conference/` was acquired *under `VL-LEGACY-CORPUS-2026-08-10` itself*, `networkMode: "consented"`, for an Apache-2.0 repository — then `admission.json` records `decision: "not-admitted"` because "The first admission gate — MIT LICENSE file content at the exact pinned revision — fails", and `source.json` says "Bound bytes are not an admission." Conversely `angular-fuxa`, carried by T012 as an unattemptable "Angular-CLI era" candidate, declares `@angular/core ^14.2.12` at its pin — post-Ivy, so it is not a 13-cell candidate and is the cheapest available test of whether the Angular build wall is 13-cell-specific or lane-wide.

**Packet item 5 — no finding.** All 24 published coverage rows were checked against the reading their basis allows; every `framework` field matches the manifest at the pin. `react-verdaccio-v4-12-2` already carries `framework: "unknown"`. Only residue is the `react-` prefix in its row **id** and cache dirs — a label the row's own field contradicts in the right direction. Not fixed, per the packet.
